The test image shows young corn plants with pronounced pale yellow-white to cream striping running parallel to leaf veins against a darker green background. No pustules, spots, or fungal growth visible. Plants appear somewhat stunted. The vein-parallel chlorotic streaking is the dominant symptom.

Top candidates: Maize_streak_virus, Downy_mildew, Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus, Stewarts_wilt. Let me compare reference images.

The Maize_chlorotic_dwarf_virus shows a close-up (bottom-right) with fine parallel pale streaks on taller plants. Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma shows red-purple anthocyanin striping on dried material — clearly different.

**Key observations from test image:**
- Young corn plants viewed from above
- Broad, continuous pale cream/white stripes running parallel to veins on most leaves
- Plants still retain significant green tissue alongside the pale stripes
- No pustules, discrete lesions, fungal growth, or leaf distortion/curling
- Soil visible — typical young field stand

**Differentiating candidates:**
- **Maize_streak_virus**: reference shows near-complete pallor on severely affected plants; fine discontinuous dashes/flecks pattern in close-up
- **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus**: reference shows broad, longitudinal cream-white bands on leaves that still retain green tissue — matching the test image's pattern of broad stripes on a still-green background
- **Downy_mildew**: uniform yellowing with whorl curling/distortion — not matching the clear alternating stripes
- **Stewarts_wilt**: reference shows very young plants without prominent stripe pattern

The test image matches MDMV most closely: broad vein-parallel pale streaks on young plants that retain green tissue, consistent with the "irregular longitudinal stripes... broad bands occupying nearly half the leaf blade" description.
